## Current developer-value execution map — 2026-09-28

This is the existing programme owner, not a new release controller or repository-wide scheduler. Public vision: [EffortlessMetrics/ripr#1719](https://github.com/EffortlessMetrics/ripr/issues/1719). The [September 17 usefulness execution decision](https://github.com/EffortlessMetrics/ripr-swarm/issues/1693#issuecomment-5707219457) remains applicable. Current leaf comments and exact-head receipts govern active work; the [latest inspected operational checkpoint](https://github.com/EffortlessMetrics/ripr-swarm/issues/1693#issuecomment-5881551814) retains the existing #4439, #4466, #4441/#4000 and #4357 writers. Do not open rival implementations for those claims.

### Source reconciliation

Inspected development source: `463ab445aa6fc47e1365b0e5b050aa0b042282ec`. This inspection read current source, retained evidence and all-state issue/PR history; it did not run a fresh repair, benchmark, installed journey or mutation experiment.

Preserve delivered work rather than restarting from old unchecked issue bodies:

- Durable attempt selection, retained before inputs, status and recovery exist. The repeat-use residual is attempt-local **terminal** evidence retention, now #4572.
- `PropagationWitnessV1` and direct return/error/field admission exist; merged #3547 is delivered work. The bounded effect/call observer residual is #4575, not another witness type.
- The boundary-gap case study and `boundary_gap_closure.rs` require repo-exposure/outcome closure. #3165 closed through #4674 (`f654882c724e8c4fac4736e95b603eac3720ebba`): its isolated `CARGO_BIN_EXE_ripr` copy, cross-projection transaction and harness-owned focused-execution controls are delivered characterization. That copy is not archive admission or public-install proof. #4510/#4516 retain the archive-admitted literal installed CLI row; #2335 retains real LSP/packaged VSIX composition.
- #3806 has retained real release judgments and targeted runtime observations. #4578 fills the missing production-quiet and actual-actionability observation strata without replacing that panel.
- #3795/#3837 delivered cache/phase observability. Updated #1578 reuses it for a repeatable saved-edit sequence; historical timing figures are not current benchmarks.
- The governed Rust corpus still has `cases: []`. That is a missing real-attempt denominator, not proof that no useful diagnostic has ever existed or that every historical exclusion still fails on current main.

### Immediate outcome sequence

```text
#3074: observe the three retained exact real opportunities with one current analyzer
    ├─ complete canonical route → #3075: first authorized real test-only attempt
    └─ no complete route → smallest evidenced producer repair → replay the same opportunity

#3075 and installed transaction qualification
    → #1702: five unique real opportunities across at least three repositories
    → #1560: the existing twenty-attempt governed corpus
```

**#3074 does not wait for #4570, the full #3160 programme, terminal-retention work, public publication or K.** Capture observations under the existing contract; adapt their representation later without rerunning merely for formatting. A development-build observation is not a public-install qualification. Current scope/authorization and immutable consumer/analyzer inputs remain required.

Reuse the landed controlled flagship #3165/#4674 characterization in #4516 and #2335; it cannot substitute for #3075 or count as a real-repository opportunity. An unsuccessful or limited real attempt is retained evidence, not a row to discard.

### Bounded implementation and proof packets

| Developer problem | Existing authority | Current bounded packet |
| --- | --- | --- |
| We cannot tell where ordinary opportunities stop | #3076 / #1560 | #4570 — derive the route-yield ladder from typed, cohort-bound observations; do not inflate attempts |
| Finishing another repair loses the earlier result | #2927 | #4572 — retain terminal after/verify/receipt evidence per attempt; global files remain compatibility projections |
| An assertion can be unrelated to the changed effect | #3161 / #1543 / #4404 | #4575 — one direct effect/call family with exact source→sink→observer binding |
| No suitable existing test means no repair route | #3162 | #4576 — first exact new integration-test target; no blanket production-file permission for inline tests |
| Quiet findings and repair offers are not independently measured | #3164 / #3806 | #4578 — reuse retained judgments and separately observe production classification and canonical actionability |
| Useful, wrong or impractical advice disappears before an attempt | #1619 | #4585 — explicit local result-bound usefulness receipts, with no automatic suppression or policy change |
| Normal saved edits have unpredictable cost or duplicate output | #1578 / #3795 / #3796 | Updated #1578 — cold/warm repeated-edit sequence, semantic parity, work counts, delivery and host-bound latency |
| The flagship archive-admitted literal installed loop remains unqualified | Landed #3165/#4674; #2929 / #4510 / #4516 | #4516 — reuse landed transaction controls, consume actual shared admission, follow public emitted commands and retain separately attributed actual focused execution; #2335 consumes the row for LSP/VSIX composition |

The new leaves are rolling work without milestone admission. A parent reference expresses ownership, not a requirement to finish every parent programme before the leaf can start. Admit producer expansion to a candidate only when current evidence establishes the required product predicate. The first real repair must not wait for every proposed effect, helper and insertion family.

### Existing owners kept intact

- #3215 owns ordinary helper/string activation satisfiability and the distinction between missing user proof and unresolved analyzer proof. Use observed cases to select its next family; no duplicate broad syntax campaign.
- #2928/#2929 own the shared editor transaction and packaged parity; #1613/#1614/#1906 own discovery, preflight and typed operational routes. Their delivered portions must be reconciled before implementation.
- #4000, #4307, #4387, #4323, #4541, #4536, #4382, #4542 and #4538 retain their individual root, artifact, guidance, identity, cache and diff contracts. Current PRs and source determine what remains; this list does not declare every historical bug freshly reproduced.
- #4357 and #3088 retain standard-client/MCP work; #1579 measures only clients actually exercised. No revival of a custom public agent protocol.
- #3751/#3752 retain the intervention-value and verification-allocation studies. This programme does not infer avoided CI runs or authorize skipping verification from static closure.
- #4508 and its existing installed language-journey leaves remain the current composition proof. Python/TypeScript expansion uses its existing language and external-cohort owners, not a second language roadmap here.

### What the trials must decide

Measure route availability, independently reviewed target/discriminator correctness, ability to complete the transaction without hidden help, actual test execution, static movement, elapsed/attention cost and optional mutation observations separately. Report every selected limitation, timeout, wrong target, abandoned attempt and missing result with its denominator.

The default result should be one bounded next action per independent semantic repair, with full evidence available—not an arbitrary fixed warning cap that hides distinct repairs. Distinguish change-caused weakness from pre-existing debt. A useful limitation is a valid product result but not a successful repair. Feedback is not analyzer truth; a passing test is not automatically a discriminating test; static closure is not execution or merge approval.

#1702 should record questions, manual artifact/path handling, commands/clicks, whether the recommended test belongs at the stated site, whether its expected result has an independent behavioral basis, and whether the developer would retain the repair. Later independent repeat use remains distinct from the internal five-attempt pilot. No external contact or repository write is implied by this issue map.

### Handoff and completion discipline

Each leaf provides exact inspected and exercised subjects, reused authorities, discriminating positive/negative controls, acceptance, rollback and explicit nonclaims. Existing source publication and current 0.11 qualification proceed under their own owners. No new release scope, support tier, required CI lane, global scheduler, credentials or public channel is changed by this map.

---

## Program identity

```text
program_id = ripr-usable-workable-release-ready
release_authority = false
candidate_freeze = false
version_change = false
publish = false
```

## Context

RIPR now has much of the right substrate: canonical diagnostics, producer-backed witness projection, actionable/full profiles, stable diagnostic identity, last-known-good snapshots, explicit root authority, saved-workspace refresh coalescing and cancellation, causal PR attribution, and a deterministic diagnostic-budget evaluator.

The remaining work should not be treated as one release train or one active goal. It is a portfolio of dependency-aware lanes that progressively improve:

1. **Usability** — a developer can install/start RIPR, save a change, receive one honest canonical diagnostic or limitation, inspect the exact evidence and related test site, refresh, and shut down cleanly.
2. **Workability** — an IDE or coding agent can repeat the loop with bounded payloads, pull/push parity, typed snapshot-bound queries, honest failure recovery, and no artifact archaeology or prose scraping.
3. **Release readiness** — one exact SHA has governed real-repository/client evidence, reproducible no-publish artifact/install proof, a current support matrix, and explicit limitations.

This program does **not** freeze a candidate, bump a version, create a tag, publish a crate/extension/binary, or authorize a release.

## Current foundation

Already landed foundations include:

- canonical semantic diagnostics and root-independent delivery identity;
- discriminator witness and fix-site projection across diagnostics, hover, packets, and actions;
- actionable/full diagnostic profiles;
- last-known-good snapshot retention and typed analysis health;
- explicit root authority, config reload, coalescing, supersession, and cooperative cancellation;
- canonical base/head causal attribution and gate projection;
- deterministic diagnostic-budget contract;
- solo-maintainer bot-review → repair → required gate → merge operating doctrine.

## Historical merge front

The original July sequence is retained below for provenance. Live issue state verified on 2026-09-08: #1629, #1671, #1669, and #1670 are all closed. They are not current writer prerequisites. Closure state alone is not fresh execution proof; inspect their retained changes and receipts when a new claim depends on them.

1. #1629 — false all-clear correction.
2. #1671 — complete analysis-input identity.
3. #1669 — pull diagnostics and analysis-input-bound result identity.
4. #1670 — typed review-comments phase/timeout receipt.

## Original work waves

These waves preserve the original program design. They are not a current priority queue: reconcile each linked issue and its existing PRs against current repository source truth before selecting work. The program acceptance below remains the outcome contract.

### Wave 1 — Usable standard editor

- Ratify #1622.
- Implement #1625 and #1626.
- Implement #1628, then #1661 PR A/B/C.
- Implement #1662 and #1615.
- Exit: VS Code and the generic framed client complete save → diagnostic/limitation → hover/related test → refresh → shutdown with honest stale/failure behavior.

### Wave 2 — Workable bounded interface

- Finish #1582 through the child issues linked from this program.
- Complete #1599 → #1602 → #1603 and #1605.
- Complete #1604 through the child issues linked from this program.
- Implement #1663 over producer facts from #1658/#1660.
- Exit: finite passive output, explicit overflow, typed complete retrieval, stale continuation/action rejection, typed timeout receipts, and no mandatory artifact search.

### Wave 3 — Real usefulness

- Continue #1601/#1658/#1660 until a real governed candidate has an exact discriminator, safe test target, verification route, and before/after movement receipt.
- Run the first bounded cross-client pilot under #1579.
- Expand the governed corpus only after the receipt shape is stable.

### Wave 4 — Progressive release readiness

- Exercise #1630.
- Run the exact-SHA no-publish package/binary/VSIX/install rehearsal.
- Generate a current readiness snapshot from evidence; do not produce a ship/no-ship verdict or candidate freeze.
- Improve documentation, support matrix, diagnostic catalog, recovery paths, and known-limit disclosures from measured evidence.

## Concurrency and ownership

Codex should treat this as a portfolio:

- One mutation writer per Work-ID and branch.
- Only one writer at a time in overlapping `lsp/backend.rs`, `lsp/state.rs`, `lsp/diagnostics.rs`, or shared protocol DTOs.
- Read-only scouts/reviewers may run in parallel.
- Analyzer/producer work, timeout-receipt work, documentation/catalog work, and artifact rehearsal may proceed concurrently when ownership is disjoint.
- Resume and finish existing PRs before opening replacement branches.
- Bot findings are verified and either fixed or dispositioned; no external approval is required.

## Program acceptance

The program may be considered complete when:

- no no-snapshot, stale, failed, limited, overflowed, or wrong-root state can render as clean;
- standard and enhanced clients receive only negotiated actions;
- all projected source locations are encoding-correct and snapshot-bound;

```text
→ currentness/comparability validation
→ static movement verification
→ receipt
→ one terminal attempt state
```

RIPR owns the plumbing. The human or external agent still owns the edit.


- create one `RepairAttemptId`;
- atomically write the attempt manifest and pre-edit artifacts;
- print the attempt ID, current state, selected test/fix site, edit cage, and exact next command;
- retain the current low-level artifacts for inspection and compatibility;

Representative next command:

```bash
ripr agent repair --root . --attempt <attempt-id> --phase after
```

- re-read the manifest and canonical producer artifacts;
- validate root, repository, base/head, config/profile/input, gap/seam, binary, and snapshot currentness;
- capture the post-edit observation;
- run the existing static `agent verify` and receipt-producing paths through their canonical APIs;
- update the manifest atomically;

```text
state

config/profile/mode/input identity

gap/seam/canonical-item identity
allowed_edit_surface

packet/brief identity
analysis-outcome identity
after artifact identity/digest
verify identity/digest/status
receipt identity/digest/status

```

Distinguish operational state from movement result.

```text

awaiting_edit
ready_to_finish
stale
incomparable
failed
```

```text

improved
unchanged
regressed
limited
```

- A non-default attempt/workflow directory is explicit and resumable.

- Re-running a completed phase is idempotent or returns a typed already-complete result.

- Root, base, config, profile, producer, or repository movement produces a typed stale/incomparable result and a precise restart route.
- Artifact-path details remain inspectable but are not required command-line plumbing for the ordinary path.

- The edit remains external; no `--edit-command`, shell hook, generated whole test, or automatic source edit.

- Paths remain root-contained and traversal-safe.

## Current premise

Source inspection at `463ab445aa6fc47e1365b0e5b050aa0b042282ec`; this is a documented repeat-use limitation, not a newly executed reproduction.

[`docs/REPAIR_ATTEMPT.md`](https://github.com/EffortlessMetrics/ripr-swarm/blob/463ab445aa6fc47e1365b0e5b050aa0b042282ec/docs/REPAIR_ATTEMPT.md) already describes durable attempt IDs, retained before artifacts, exact continuation, currentness checks, status, and refusal recovery. Do not rebuild them.

The same contract says `target/ripr/reports/agent-receipt.json` holds one receipt. Finishing B replaces A's receipt; status reports A as superseded instead of being able to read its earlier outcome. [`RIPR-SPEC-0011`](https://github.com/EffortlessMetrics/ripr-swarm/blob/463ab445aa6fc47e1365b0e5b050aa0b042282ec/docs/specs/RIPR-SPEC-0011-llm-work-loop.md) explicitly calls the old reading `unconfirmed`. Current status projection is in [`app/agent_status.rs`](https://github.com/EffortlessMetrics/ripr-swarm/blob/463ab445aa6fc47e1365b0e5b050aa0b042282ec/crates/ripr/src/app/agent_status.rs); attempt authority is `app/repair_attempt.rs`.

A developer should not have to archive global artifacts between otherwise valid repairs. An attempt ID must continue to identify its own completed result after another attempt, a process restart, or a compatibility-output refresh.

All-state searches for attempt-local retention and receipt/attempt work found the broad #2927 contract and Python cohort #3557; this leaf owns ordinary shared attempt terminal retention, not another attempt lifecycle or Python execution engine.

## One-PR outcome

Retain the authoritative terminal result and its verification/receipt dependencies under the existing attempt directory, with manifest-bound paths and digests. Repository-global outputs remain compatibility projections and cannot become the sole surviving copy of an attempt result.

Use existing role-based retained-artifact machinery and atomic-file helpers. No new database, ledger service, command family, or parallel editor state machine.

## Publication and reading law

1. Resolve the exact attempt and retain the current before commitment unchanged.
2. Build the terminal static-result bundle through the existing after/verify/receipt authorities. Retain only the evidence needed to validate that result, not the whole workspace or cache.
3. Publish the attempt-local files and manifest reference in an order that prevents a manifest claiming success before its required bytes are durable. Multi-file atomicity cannot be assumed from independent renames.
4. Update compatibility projections separately. Their later replacement, deletion, or failure must not erase the attempt-local result or make a different attempt authoritative.
5. `agent status` and shared result readers prefer exact attempt-local evidence. Validate the selected attempt, hashes, source scope, and result kind before projecting it.
6. An old result can remain historically valid while no longer current for today's HEAD. Expose both facts; do not turn retained history into current proof.

Document crash recovery for each publish boundary. Retrying may return already-finished/current result or a typed recoverable state, but must not run the test again, issue contradictory closure, or replace committed evidence silently.

## Compatibility

Old manifests without terminal retention remain readable at their earned strength. They may use a still-present exact matching legacy receipt, but a missing or superseded receipt remains unconfirmed. Do not backfill an old outcome from today's global file or infer it from a terminal-state name.

The trust-bound Python verify route currently has additional repository-global apply/verification restrictions. Do not silently relax them or add execution authority. Reuse the shared retention facility where compatible; explicitly document any remaining Python-specific restriction under #3557.

## First falsifier

Finish attempt A, capture its result, then finish B with a different gap and outcome. Restart the process and inspect A. A must still return A's retained outcome, not B's result and not an artificial loss-of-receipt state. This is the discriminating repeat-use test; two independently successful single-attempt tests are insufficient.

## Required controls

- Two attempts for different gaps; two attempts for the same seam with distinct IDs.
- Global receipt rewritten, removed, malformed, or bound to B while reading A.
- Attempt-local artifact removed, payload changed, wrong digest, wrong root, or path escape: typed unavailable/corrupt, never global fallback to another attempt.
- Failure between each terminal-file publication and manifest update; restart produces an honest result or explicit recovery.
- Manifest says finished but required result is missing: not successful closure.
- Static movement improved/closed with project execution not-run or failed: retain separate axes.
- HEAD/config/analyzer movement: historical validity does not become current proof.
- Legacy manifest and exact matching legacy receipt; legacy superseded receipt cannot be reconstructed.
- Linux and Windows path/atomic replacement controls using existing platform harnesses.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Completing a later repair never destroys access to an earlier retained terminal result.
- [ ] CLI and editor readers consume the same exact-attempt artifact authority.
- [ ] Before commitments remain immutable; terminal evidence is content-bound and safely published.
- [ ] Crash/retry and compatibility behavior are explicit and fixture-backed.
- [ ] No extra manual archive/copy command is required between ordinary repairs.
- [ ] Existing cage, currentness, runtime/static separation, and no-implicit-execution rules remain intact.
- [ ] Docs and the schema's compatibility policy describe retained history versus currentness accurately.

## Proof and rollback

Start with the A→B→inspect-A public CLI control, then focused attempt/status/persistence tests, relevant output-contract and package journey checks, and current PR gates. Require actual nonzero test execution; implementation records the concrete test names. Reuse #2929/#4510 qualification machinery where appropriate rather than adding an always-on full workspace lane.

Rollback preserves retained attempt directories and makes old readers report unsupported terminal fields honestly. No cleanup command may delete historical receipts as cache. This issue does not authorize a release, support promotion, consumer-repository edit, or change to the current 0.11 denominator.
